newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Difference among Albanian parties very small-Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Difference among Albanian parties very small-Prodi.

text.p: Italian Prime minister Romano Prodi said on Wednesday differences among Albanian political parties over holding elections were being narrowed in marathon talks and that an agreement could be reached within a few days.
"The differences among the parties are very small now," Prodi said during a news conference in Budapest.

"It is a problem to try to cancel the last misunderstandings, misinterpretations and the deep degree of no confidence among the Albanian parties but (European envoy Franz) Vranitzky is working on that and we are backing him.
"I am confident that we can have some positive steps in the next days or so," Prodi said during a joint news conference with Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn on the second day of bilateral talks.
He made the comments as Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino plunged into fresh talks on Wednesday to end a crisis jeopardising elections planned for June 29.

Vranitzky had warned Albania's politicians to solve a deadlock over electoral ground-rules by the end of Tuesday or face the risk of losing international aid needed to overcome near-anarchy afflicting the poor Balkan country.
Late-night efforts by Fino yielded no agreement but he began a new round of negotiations with parties in his so-called national unity government on Wednesday morning.
Italy, which commands multinational troops protecting aid supplies and maintaining order in some of Albania's most lawless areas, has said it may pull out if elections do not go ahead.
